Let's begin the lesson on PROGRAMMABLE UNIJUNCTION TRANSISTORS (PUTs).......
Although the PUT performs the same functions as the UJT, its construction is different. The PUT uses 4 semiconductor layers and a gate. The UJT uses 3 semiconductor layers and two bases.
The PUT structure is similar to a four layer SCR except for the gate. Notice on the PUT, the gate is connected to the N region adjacent to the anode.
DISCUSSION
In the UJT relaxation oscillator, R1, C1 and the intrinsic standoff ratio of the circuit controls the frequency of oscillation.
C1 charges through R1 until it reaches Vp, which turns "ON" the UJT. This lowers the resistance between terminals E and B1. C1 rapidly discharges to Vv through R3, turning "OFF" the UJT.
DEFINITION
INTRINSIC STANDOFF RATIO - This ratio is a measure of the internal resistance of the two base junctions with reference to the voltage required to bias the emitter.

When C1 reaches (Vg + 0.7) or Vp, the PUT turns "ON" and C1 rapidly discharges through the negative resistance of the PUT and R2 until it reaches Vv and the PUT turns "OFF" and the charging cycle of C1 starts over...
The waveforms generated by the PUT relaxation oscillator are developed across C1 (sawtooth) and R2 (pulses).
Like the UJT, the frequency of oscillation can be varied by adjusting R1, or by changing the value of C1.
The resistance ratio of R3 and R4 programs the intrinsic standoff ratio, which controls the value of Vp.
